finding.classification: pre-existing scheduling-sensitive instrumentation limitation; not a demonstrated pagination regression or application read/heap violation
finding.source_identity: git diff bd149f8..6861d8f -- e2e/scripts/index_acceptance_bounds.exs is empty. Current collector logic predates pagination; dd21d80 added high priority only.
finding.mechanism_supported: A high-priority collector on one scheduler can receive more than 512 asynchronous events while other schedulers continue producers. Priority and off-heap mailbox placement do not provide backpressure. Both GC/storage candidates still overflowed without read/event/worker-heap/60-second overruns.
finding.mechanism_not_proven: No direct evidence identifies whether original local full-lane overflow was OS descheduling, trace-delivery burst, collector GC, or another pause. Pure-control timing implicates scheduling sensitivity but does not isolate the underlying host mechanism.

source_observations: bounds.exs:179-211 creates isolated high-priority private collector; caller inventory/history and unrelated owner mailbox are not intentionally copied into it.
bounds.exs:223-271 creates request worker capped at 128 MiB; tracing is confined to request worker plus configured native PID.
bounds.exs:273-294 initializes exact counts/GC/heap and original 60000ms deadline.
bounds.exs:342-357 uses arity-only trace and constant token/label messages: keys, source values, command data and return values are not emitted.
bounds.exs:371-379 checks mailbox twice per loop at512, total events at4*read_limit+4096, sample deadline and heap.
bounds.exs:382-430 stops tracees in session and uses per-tracee delivered barriers before accepting sample.
bounds.exs:438-481 accounts every exact-call/GC event and rejects forbidden calls. GC start/end are each counted as events; native GC is not traced.

bounds.exs:485-512 samples worker memory only in receive after1ms path; it may not sample during continuous events, but worker GC blocks/final heap remain tracked. This is not established as the mailbox failure cause.

Existing CPU probe exercises one-read success; its explicit collector suspension produces600 trace events and confirms512 rejection. This task preserved but did not rerun that probe against rejected candidates.

probe_design.runtime: Host Elixir1.18.5 / OTP28, +S4:4. No Mix, Concord runtime, dependency compilation, server or native extension.
probe_design.shape: Synchronous request worker -> Engine -> VSR -> own native process -> Core -> dispatch. Four real exact-call trace events per logical read, plus actual worker GC events. Each completed request returns1000 entries and calls Bounds.record_read for every returned value.
probe_design.counts_checked_on_every_success: Each of engine/vsr/core/dispatch equals actual reads; trace_events equals4*reads+gc_events; output_entries equals1000; original check_sample! and all original collector guards remain in use.
probe_design.payloads: Tiny record and second realistic map with32 child references, label and metadata key; raw payload/key data are never traced or logged.
probe_design.failure_diagnostics: bounds-observed.exs changes only overflow diagnostics before the original guard. It classifies messages by event type and reports numeric counts, fixed counters, process memory/priority, barriers and runqueue lengths. It does not change any original bound or guard.

escalation.unresolved_question: Can a process-local collector change reliably retain the original hard512 asynchronous-message rejection while fully accounting up to136260 events, without request pacing/acks, changed producer scheduling, dropped/batched-away evidence, retries or relaxed read/heap/deadline bounds?

More heuristic process flags would not establish bounded correctness or address an externally descheduled collector.
